newsitem.title: UK: London gold looks for support after overnight fall.
newsitem.headline: London gold looks for support after overnight fall.

text.p: Precious metals prices were turning lower in Europe on Thursday but dealers were reasonably sure there was enough interest around to prevent a serious drop.
"There are enquiries under the market and we are looking for gold to be in a $318-$324 (per ounce) range today," one dealer said.

The price had been picking up from 12-year lows around $313 plumbed earlier this month following the announcement by the Reserve Bank of Australia that it had sold 167 tonnes of metal from reserves during the preceding six months.
Gold fixed at $321.80 compared with $324.90 on Wednesday afternoon and a close then of $324.50/$325.00.

Prices turned weaker in New York in light volume as the dollar strengthened in response to the second day of Congressional testimony by Federal Reserve Board chairman Alan Greenspan on the state of the U.S. economy.

His conclusions that slowing growth and low inflation horizons removed the need for immediate interest rate rises lifted the U.S. bond and stock markets while reducing the attractions of gold as a store of value.
More directly pertinent for gold were fresh selling by funds and producers out of Australia and rumours of European central bank sales although dealers were largely dismissive of them.
"There have been a lot of rumours about central banks," one dealer said flatly.
Hong Kong prices fell to a low of just over $320.00 as local speculators caught the bearish tendency.
At these levels short covering and physical purchases came in to add a little firmness by the local close.
In the background was a statement from Anglogold that due to low prices it would review marginal shafts at its Freegold, the world's largest gold mine.
Platinum and palladium were easier too despite Russia's export organisations being still riven with power struggles following the end of contracted exports last December.
Russia is the largest export of palladium and second largest supplier of platinum after South Africa.
"There is more metal around so lease rates are easing," one dealer said. Even so quotes of around 80 percent for short term borrowing of palladium were also mentioned on Thursday.
Platinum was indicated at $415.00/$418.00 down a dollar and palladium was at $196.00/$199.00, 40 cents easier.
